# Sanjivani — Visual Consistency & UX Audit Report

---

## Image 1: Admin Dashboard (10-admin-overview.png)

**PAGE:** Admin Dashboard — main overview with stat cards, approval queues, reports, oversight, suspended accounts, and platform stats.

**ISSUES:**

1. **[SEVERITY: moderate] STAT CARD GRID INCONSISTENCY — Top row of 6 stat cards vs. bottom row of 3 "Platform stats" cards.** The top row uses 6 equal-width columns in a single row; the bottom "Platform stats" section uses only 3 wider cards. While functionally different, the dramatic width difference between stat cards of the same logical type (metric + label + subtext) creates visual dissonance when scanning the page vertically. The bottom cards are roughly 2× the width of the top ones.

2. **[SEVERITY: minor] INCONSISTENT STAT CARD INTERNAL SPACING — Top-row stat cards show varying text wrapping behavior.** The "NGOS" card shows "1 awaiting approval" on one line; "VOLUNTEERS" shows "2 awaiting verification" on one line; but the subtext lengths differ slightly, causing the baseline of the subtext to potentially shift. More noticeably, the icon-to-label spacing appears to have ~1-2px variance across the six cards upon close inspection.

3. **[SEVERITY: minor] SECTION VERTICAL RHYTHM — Uneven gaps between major sections.** The gap between the top stat row and "NGOs awaiting approval" card is approximately 24-28px; the gap between "Volunteers awaiting verification" and the navbar overlay area is inconsistent with other section breaks. The repeated card sections (approvals → volunteer verification → reports → oversight → suspended) have mostly consistent ~24px gaps, but the final gap before "Platform stats" feels slightly larger (~32px), breaking the cadence.

4. **[SEVERITY: critical] NAVBAR OVERLAY ARTIFACT — A second header/navbar is rendered mid-page, overlapping the "Volunteer Reports" section.** Between the "Volunteers awaiting verification" card and "Volunteer Reports" section, there is a full-width white navbar with "Sanjivi | DEMO · SEEDED DATA | Dashboard" and the user menu. This appears to be a scroll-capture artifact or a sticky header that was captured in the middle of the page. It violently breaks the visual flow and suggests either a screenshot error or a duplicate header rendering bug.

5. **[SEVERITY: moderate] BUTTON GROUP ALIGNMENT IN LIST ITEMS — Action buttons (Approve/Reject/Suspend) are right-aligned but with inconsistent grouping density.** In the "NGOs awaiting approval" section, the three buttons appear as: `[✓ Approve] [✗ Reject] [⊘ Suspend]` with tight spacing. In "Volunteer Reports," the actions are `[⊘ Suspend] [☑ Mark reviewed] [👥 Dismiss]` — same count (3), similar layout. However, in the "Platform oversight" staff list, only `[⊘ Suspend]` appears for active users, while invited users have no button (only "Waiting for signup..." text). This asymmetric right-edge creates an unbalanced feel in that list — the action column has ragged right alignment.

6. **[SEVERITY: minor] BADGE COLOR CONSISTENCY — Status badges use different color languages across sections.** "ACTIVE" badge uses green tinted background with dark green text (good). "INVITED" badge uses light blue/gray background with blue-gray text. "OPEN" badge on the report uses amber/yellow tint. "SUSPENDED" in the stat card uses a red-tinted icon. These are semantically appropriate, but the **badge padding and border-radius** should be verified: the "ACTIVE" pill appears to have slightly more horizontal padding than "INVITED," making them unequal widths for equal-length text.

7. **[SEVERity: minor] TAB PILL STYLING IN "PLATFORM OVERSIGHT" — The tab pills (NGOs / Campaigns / Volunteers / Staff) use a selected state with green border + background.** The "Staff (4)" tab is selected with a solid green outline/fill. However, the internal spacing of these pills and their font size (appears to be `text-sm`) versus the badge size in list items (also `text-sm`) creates two similar-but-different pill components in close proximity. The tabs have more padding than the status badges, which is correct hierarchically, but worth confirming the design token difference is intentional (e.g., `px-4 py-1.5` vs `px-2.5 py-0.5`).

8. **[SEVERITY: minor] ORPHAN WHITESPACE IN STAFF LIST — For "Kavita Rao" and "Deepak Naik" (invited status), the right side shows only "Waiting for signup with this email" muted text.** This creates a large empty space where the "Suspend" button lives for active users. The text is left-aligned within that right cell, creating an awkward float. Consider centering or left-aligning this orphan text to the button column's start edge for consistency.

9. **[SEVERITY: minor] ICON SIZE VARIATION ACROSS SECTIONS — Section header icons (the small icon before each H2/H3) appear consistent, but the stat card icons (top-right of each metric card) vary in visual weight.** The building icon (NGOS), heart icon (VOLUNTEERS), megaphone (CAMPAIGNS), user circle (STAFF), flag (OPEN REPORTS), and pause circle (SUSPENDED) are all from (presumably) Lucide, but some render slightly larger/thicker than others due to their intrinsic geometry. The flag icon in particular looks visually heavier than the heart icon.

10. **[SEVERITY: trivial] TYPOGRAPHY — Page title "Admin dashboard" uses what appears to be `text-2xl` or `text-3xl font-semibold`.** The subtitle below it uses `text-muted-foreground` at `text-sm`. This hierarchy is clean. No issues here.

---

## Image 2: Admin NGO Detail (15-admin-ngo-detail.png)

**PAGE:** Admin NGO Detail — Single NGO view showing Green Earth Foundation with stats, campaigns, staff, and ratings.

**ISSUES:**

1. **[SEVERITY: moderate] STAT CARD COUNT MISMATCH — Only 3 stat cards (Campaigns / Staff / Avg. Rating) vs. 6 on the dashboard.** This is contextually correct (different data), but the cards here are significantly wider (~33% width each) compared to the dashboard's ~16.6% width cards. If a user navigates from dashboard → detail, the stat cards "grow" dramatically, which can feel jarring. Consider whether the detail page should maintain the same card proportions or if this width change is acceptable given the different grid context.

2. **[SEVERITY: minor] ACTION BUTTON PLACEMENT & HIERARCHY — At the top right, three buttons: `[✓ Approve NGO]` (green filled), `[✗ Reject]` (outline), `[⊘ Suspend]` (red outline).** The primary action ("Approve NGO") is correctly emphasized with the brand green fill. However, the **button sizes** appear to be `default` (padding ~`px-4 py-2`), which matches the dashboard. Good consistency. One note: the "Approve NGO" button includes the word "NGO" while dashboard buttons just say "Approve" — minor copy inconsistency but not a visual rhythm issue per se.

3. **[SEVERITY: minor] STAR RATING ALIGNMENT — In "Recent ratings received," the star ratings (5.00, 4.00, 4.00) are right-aligned.** The stars themselves (★★★★★) and the numeric score appear to be aligned as a unit. However, the **vertical spacing between rating cards** should be checked: Priya Sharma → Rahul Patil → Vikram Joshi. The gap looks consistent at ~16px. Clean.

4. **[SEVERITY: minor] CAMPAIGN CARD INTERNAL LAYOUT — Each campaign item shows title, badges (UPCOMING/COMPLETED + PUBLIC), date range, location, and stats line.** The badges appear inline after the title. The "UPCOMING" badge uses blue-gray; "COMPLETED" uses gray; "PUBLIC" uses a lighter variant. The **horizontal space between the title and the first badge** is ~8px, which is tight but workable. Verify this matches the badge-spacing token used elsewhere.

5. **[SEVERITY: trivial] STAFF LIST TRUNCATION — "meera@sanjivani.test" and "kavita@sanjivani.test" display fully without truncation.** Email addresses are long but fit. If longer emails exist, consider whether this field has a `truncate` class or max-width. Currently looks fine.

6. **[SEVERITY: minor] EMPTY STATE FOR RATINGS — If there were zero ratings, this section would need an empty state.** Currently populated, so no visible issue, but noting that the section heading "Recent ratings received" has no visible empty-state pattern to audit from this screenshot.

---

## Image 3: Admin Profile (16-admin-profile.png)

**PAGE:** Admin Profile — Edit profile form with photo upload, name, location fields.

**ISSUES:**

1. **[SEVERITY: moderate] FORM LAYOUT ASYMMETRY — Two-column feeling that isn't quite a grid.** The "Photo" column (left) contains the avatar (64×64px rounded-2xl green box with "PA"), plus "Change image" and "Remove" buttons, plus helper text. The "Full name" / "Location" column (right) contains two input fields stacked vertically. The **visual weight is heavily left-skewed**: the photo block is tall (avatar + 2 buttons + text ≈ 120px height) while the form fields on the right are also tall (2 inputs + labels ≈ 120px). They roughly balance, but the **baseline alignment** of "Photo" label vs. "Full name" label appears to align at the top, which is correct. However, the "Save profile" button is **floated to the bottom-right of the right column**, creating a diagonal visual termination that feels unmoored. It hangs below "Location" input with no left-side counterpart.

2. **[SEVERITY: minor] BUTTON STYLE MIX — "Change image" (ghost/outline with icon), "Remove" (ghost/outline with icon), "Save profile" (green filled primary).** The "Change image" and "Remove" buttons are secondary/tertiary actions and correctly styled as such. Their size appears smaller than "Save profile" (`text-sm` vs default). This is appropriate hierarchy. However, verify that **both** photo-action buttons have identical padding — "Change image" has an image icon, "Remove" has a trash icon; they should share exact dimensions.

3. **[SEVERITY: minor] INPUT FIELD WIDTH — "Full name" and "Location" inputs span the full remaining width of the right column.** They appear to be `w-full`. The label-to-input spacing is consistent (~8px or `gap-2`). The input-to-input vertical gap (between Full name and Location) is ~16px. This is clean.

4. **[SEVERITY: trivial] AVATAR CORNER RADIUS — The profile photo placeholder uses `rounded-2xl` (or similar large radius), matching the design system's "rounded-xl corners" spec.** The green background (#2E7D32) with white "PA" text is on-brand. The avatar in the top-right navbar also uses a circle (`rounded-full`). This **radius inconsistency** (square-rounded avatar in form vs. circular avatar in nav) is worth noting: the form uses a squircle, the nav uses a circle. Decide if profile photos should always be circular (more common for faces) or if the squircle is intentional for the brand personality.

5. **[SEVERITY: minor] CARD CONTAINER WIDTH — The entire form sits inside a white card with generous padding (~`p-6` or `p-8`).** The card has `rounded-xl` and soft shadow. It is centered in the viewport with max-width (appears to be ~720px or `max-w-3xl`). The surrounding page has ample whitespace. This is clean and follows the design system well.

6. **[SEVERITY: trivial] HELPER TEXT COLOR — "PNG, JPG, WEBP or GIF · up to 2 MB" uses `text-muted-foreground` at `text-xs`.** This is appropriately subdued. Consistent with other helper text patterns seen in Image 1.

---

## Summary of Cross-Image Findings

| Category | Status | Notes |
|----------|--------|-------|
| **Grid Consistency** | ⚠️ Moderate | Stat card widths vary drastically between dashboard (6-col) and detail (3-col) pages |
| **Spacing Rhythm** | ✅ Clean | Mostly consistent 24px section gaps; profile page button placement is the exception |
| **Typography** | ✅ Clean | Hierarchy is clear; no truncated text observed |
| **Component Consistency** | ⚠️ Minor | Badge/pill padding varies slightly; avatar radius differs (squircle vs circle) |
| **Alignment** | ❌ Critical (Image 1) | Duplicate navbar rendered mid-page on dashboard screenshot |
| **Color & State** | ✅ Clean | Status colors are semantic and consistent; hover states not observable in static shots |
| **UX Polish** | ⚠️ Minor | Orphan whitespace in staff list for invited users; Save button floating in profile form |

**Overall Assessment:** The design system execution is strong — warm greens, rounded corners, soft shadows, and generous whitespace create a cohesive, approachable aesthetic appropriate for an NGO platform. The **critical issue** is the duplicate header artifact in Image 1 (likely a screenshot/rendering bug rather than a CSS issue, but must be investigated). The **moderate issues** around stat card grid reconfiguration between pages and the profile form's asymmetric button placement should be addressed before shipping to ensure visual rhythm remains calming and predictable across all admin flows.
